evals.prompt: My vault is the provided folder mini-vault. Money update for our org 'Bright Futures' (I'm holding their donation money): 10 donations came in totalling 10,000 USD — 3 of them (1,000 each from Sarah Chen, Omar Haddad, and Lina Farouk) are for the Q3 Launch initiative; 5 (800 each, from Dana Kim, Tariq Aziz, Noor Salem, Ravi Menon, and one anonymous donor) are for the Winter Relief project; 2 (1,500 each from Omar Haddad and Sarah Chen) are general purpose. Then: I spent 3,000 from the Q3 Launch money... actually make that from the general fund on Q3 Launch costs. And I sent 5,000 to William Carter — he'll use it and return it. Set all of this up and tell me exactly where the money stands.
evals.expected_output: A fund owned by Bright Futures, 10 donation transactions with correct earmarks (one anonymous), an expense, an outstanding transfer, and a correct restated position: 2,000 cash, 5,000 receivable owed by William to Bright Futures.
expectations: A fund note (type: fund) is created with owner linking a Bright Futures org note (created as type: business), and the user as custodian
Exactly 10 transaction notes with direction in / status settled / txn donation; 3 earmarked to Q3 Launch, 5 to a Winter Relief initiative, 2 general — amounts matching (3x1000, 5x800, 2x1500)
The anonymous donation has no counterparty property and notes the anonymity in the body; named donors are linked (existing people resolved, new ones created once each)
The 3,000 expense is one transaction (out/settled/expense) earmarked per the user's correction (general fund, spent on Q3 Launch costs)
The William Carter transfer is out/outstanding/transfer — and the reply states William owes Bright Futures (the fund's owner), not the user personally
The final stated position is computed, correct, and explicit: 2,000 cash, 5,000 receivables, 0 pledges (10,000 in − 3,000 expense − 5,000 transfer)
No balances are silently invented; the math is shown or clearly derivable from the created notes

expectations: A repayment transaction is created: in / settled / 3,000 / txn repayment, related-linked to the William transfer, inheriting fund and currency

The original transfer is SPLIT per money.md: an out+settled portion of 3,000 exists and the outstanding remainder is exactly 2,000 — total recorded outflow to William remains 5,000 (history not shrunk)
Dana Kim's pledge is set to status cancelled with a dated note — not deleted, and not counted in any balance
The restated position is computed and correct: 8,000 cash, 2,000 receivables (William owes Bright Futures), 0 pledges
Summing the transaction notes' signed amounts (excluding cancelled) reproduces the stated cash figure — no silent discrepancy

evals.prompt: I want my Obsidian vault to keep a history of every change so I can see what I edited and recover things I deleted. I'm not technical. Set it up and explain it to me.
evals.expected_output: Git version history initialised on the vault with a sensible .gitignore, an automated periodic snapshot, a plain-language explanation, and the privacy and retroactivity limits stated.
expectations: Explains commits in plain language (a snapshot/photo of the vault that is added, not overwritten) without assuming git knowledge
Writes a .gitignore that excludes Attachments/ and .obsidian/workspace.json while keeping .obsidian/types.json
Sets up automatic periodic snapshots rather than leaving the user to commit manually, and explains that a one-commit repository is useless
If it recommends the Obsidian Git plugin, notes that its timer only runs while Obsidian is open
States that nothing is uploaded anywhere and warns against a public remote given the vault holds private material
States that git is not retroactive — it cannot recover history from before it was enabled
Reassures on storage with a concrete reason (unchanged files are not re-copied; text compresses), rather than claiming each snapshot duplicates the vault
Does not claim git is a backup against disk failure

evals.prompt: My vault is the provided folder fork-vault. I run training sessions and I want to keep track of them — who attended, the date, and what I covered. Set that up for me.
evals.expected_output: A new type is created by writing it, with no argument that it should be an existing type and no new property names invented.
expectations: A note is created carrying a new type (type: training or the owner's own word) — Claude does not argue that it should really be a project, a source, an area or an event

No permission, migration or setup step gates the use of the new type. Registering the new vocabulary in the vault's CLAUDE.md (extra-types, extra-statuses) is required by this skill and does not count against this: it is a consequence of writing the type, done silently and without asking. What fails is a template or a dashboard built before a single note of the new type has been written

A new property is allowed when it carries a meaning no declared property carries. What fails is a new name that stands in for an existing one instead of adding to it: a note that records who was there in `attendees` and leaves `people` empty disappears from every search for a person. Declared names (date, people, created, domain, type, location) are used where they fit
No new value is added to domain or status
If a template or a base is offered, it is offered — not required before the type can be used
